stories.title: FCC Drops Its Gigabit Broadband Speed Goal
stories.summary: The FCC ended its goal of gigabit internet speeds for all Americans. The agency says the old goal was unfair to slower technologies. Critics say the move lowers ambitions for broadband upgrades.
stories.whyItMatters: The change could shape how much telecom firms invest in faster networks and how regulators judge broadband progress.
whatToWatch: Watch for a replacement speed benchmark from the FCC.
Watch how ISPs adjust their network investment plans.
questions: What new goal, if any, will replace the gigabit target?
Which technologies benefit most from a lower bar?

FCC abolishes gigabit speed goal, suggesting it is unfair to slower technologies

stories.title: Framework Addresses BIOS Update That Bricked Some Laptops
stories.summary: A Framework BIOS update broke some older laptops with Ryzen 7040 chips. Users reported the update made their laptops unusable. Framework says it is working on a fix.
stories.whyItMatters: The incident tests trust in Framework's repairable, modular hardware, which depends on safe firmware updates.
whatToWatch: Watch for Framework's official fix or rollback update.
Watch for word on how many units were affected.
questions: What caused the update to brick devices?
Will affected users get replacements or refunds?

stories.title: Reverse-Lookup Service Exposed Millions of Face Photos
stories.summary: A reverse-lookup service left millions of people's face photos exposed. The photos could reportedly be searched and matched to real identities. Security researchers flagged the exposure.
stories.whyItMatters: The leak shows how face-lookup services can turn personal photos into a searchable identity risk.

stories.title: Grok Sends Gibberish Replies and Can Leak Data via Encrypted Prompts
stories.summary: xAI's Grok chatbot has been sending garbled, nonsensical responses to some users. Separately, researchers found Grok can leak user data when malicious instructions are encrypted before being sent to it. The two issues point to reliability and security gaps in the chatbot.
stories.whyItMatters: It signals that widely used AI chatbots still struggle with basic reliability and can be tricked into leaking data.
whatToWatch: Watch for xAI's explanation or fix for the gibberish output.
Watch whether the encrypted-instruction exploit gets patched.
questions: Are the two issues related?
How many users were affected by the data leak?

stories.title: SpaceX's Orbital Data Center Plans Raise E-Waste Concerns
stories.summary: SpaceX's plans for data centers in orbit would create a new kind of electronic waste, a report says. Hardware in orbit is harder to repair, recycle, or safely dispose of than hardware on Earth.
stories.whyItMatters: As companies push computing into orbit, space may inherit the tech industry's unresolved e-waste problem, with fewer fixes available.
whatToWatch: Watch for details on SpaceX's orbital data center timeline.
Watch for any regulatory or environmental response.
questions: Who would be responsible for orbital e-waste?
How would defunct orbital hardware be disposed of?

stories.title: Amazon Delivery Drones Are Dropping Packages in Pools and Ponds
stories.summary: Some Amazon delivery drones have dropped packages into pools and ponds instead of yards. The reports come as Amazon aims to expand drone delivery to 500 US neighborhoods by the end of 2026.
stories.whyItMatters: Delivery accuracy problems could slow Amazon's drone expansion and invite more safety or regulatory scrutiny.
whatToWatch: Watch whether Amazon fixes landing accuracy before its 2026 goal.

stories.whyItMatters: Roblox has a huge child user base, and repeated regulatory pressure could force platform-wide safety changes or penalties.
